examples.en: I worked all day under the scorching sun.

examples.ko: 한여름 뙤약볕에 운동장에 서 있었더니 어지러웠어요.
examples.en: I stood on the playground in the midsummer sun and felt dizzy.

examples.ko: 뙤약볕이 내리쬐는 길을 모자 없이 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked along the sun-baked road without a hat.

examples.ko: 농부들은 뙤약볕을 피해 아침 일찍 밭에 나가요.
examples.en: Farmers go to the fields early in the morning to avoid the blazing sun.
The ice cream melted quickly because of the blazing sun.
Even in the scorching sun, the cheering squad held its place.

explain: 여름 한낮에 강하게 내리쬐는 햇볕이에요. '햇볕'보다 덥고 고생스러운 느낌이 있어서 '뙤약볕 아래', '뙤약볕이 내리쬐다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '땡볕'도 있어요.

phrases.example: 뙤약볕 아래에서 공을 찼더니 너무 더웠어요.
phrases.en: I played ball under the scorching sun and got very hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그늘 없이 강한 햇볕을 받는 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for places with no shade under strong sun.

phrases.en: At midday the sun beats down, so walking is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇볕이 강하게 비추는 모습을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for strong sun beating down.

phrases.en: Don't stand in the blazing sun for long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뙤약볕'과 비슷한 말로, 더 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, a bit more casual.

explain_en: It is the intense sun beating down at midday in summer. It feels hotter and more punishing than '햇볕', and is used in patterns like '뙤약볕 아래' and '뙤약볕이 내리쬐다'. A similar word is '땡볕'.

t90.ax: I worked all day under the scorching sun.

examples.en: The heavy rain turned the whole street into a sea of water.
A bathroom pipe burst and the house is flooded.
After the typhoon passed, the village turned into a flooded area.

examples.ko: 아이가 욕조 물을 틀어 놓아 바닥이 물바다였어요.
examples.en: The child left the bath water running, and the floor was covered in water.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 물바다 같던 운동장이 말랐어요.
examples.en: When the rain stopped, the schoolyard that looked like a lake dried up.

examples.ko: 물바다에 잠긴 차를 보고 말문이 막혔어요.
examples.en: I was speechless seeing the car submerged in the floodwater.

explain: 물이 넘쳐서 바닥이나 땅이 온통 물에 덮인 모습을 말해요. 큰 홍수뿐 아니라 집에서 물을 쏟았을 때도 '완전 물바다야'처럼 조금 과장해서 말해요. '홍수'는 큰 자연재해 이름이고, '물바다'는 그 모습을 그리는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 비가 계속 와서 운동장이 물바다로 변했어요.
phrases.en: It kept raining, and the playground turned into a sea of water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 괜찮던 곳이 물에 덮일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place that was fine gets covered in water.

phrases.en: I knocked over a cup, and my desk is completely flooded.
phrases.nuance_ko: '온통'을 붙여 물이 넓게 퍼진 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 온통 stresses that the water has spread everywhere.

phrases.en: Wow, the bathroom is soaked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈앞 모습을 보고 놀라서 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds like a reaction to seeing the scene in front of you.

explain_en: It describes ground or floors completely covered with overflowing water. It is used for big floods but also, a bit exaggerated, when you spill water at home, as in '완전 물바다야'. '홍수' names a big natural disaster, while '물바다' paints the picture of how it looks.

examples.ko: 겨울이면 산짐승이 먹이를 찾아 마을로 내려와요.
examples.en: In winter, mountain animals come down to the village looking for food.
I heard a wild animal's cry at night and was scared.
You must not feed wild mountain animals.
If you meet a wild animal on the mountain path, quietly avoid it.

examples.ko: 산짐승의 발자국이 눈 위에 찍혀 있었어요.
examples.en: A wild animal's footprints were pressed in the snow.

examples.ko: 이 산에는 어떤 산짐승들이 사는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder what kinds of wild animals live on this mountain.

explain: 산에 사는 야생 짐승을 가리켜요. '짐승'이 붙어서 새나 곤충보다 멧돼지, 노루 같은 네발 동물이 먼저 떠올라요. 일상에서는 '야생동물'이 더 일반적이고, '산짐승'은 시골이나 산 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Many wild animals live in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산짐승'보다 일상에서 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이고, 산이 아닌 곳의 동물에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily life than '산짐승', and not limited to mountains.

phrases.en: I'm worried I might meet a wild animal in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산길에서 야생 짐승과 마주치는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for running into a wild animal on a mountain path.

phrases.en: You have to watch out for wild animals at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산에서 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase used when giving a warning in the mountains.
phrases.en_equiv: to watch out for mountain animals

explain_en: It refers to wild beasts that live in the mountains. Because of '짐승' (beast), four-legged animals like wild boars and roe deer come to mind more than birds or insects. '야생동물' is more common in general, while '산짐승' appears more in talk about the countryside and mountains.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 제방이 무너질까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It's raining a lot, and I'm worried the embankment will collapse.

examples.ko: 강 제방을 따라 산책하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people walk along the river embankment.

examples.ko: 제방에 구멍이 생겨서 물이 새고 있어요.
examples.en: A hole formed in the levee, and water is leaking out.
Cherry blossoms bloomed along the embankment road.
They started embankment construction to prepare for floods.
I can see people fishing on top of the embankment.

explain: 강이나 바다의 물을 막으려고 쌓은 둑을 말해요. 일상에서는 '둑'이라고 많이 하고, 뉴스나 공사 이야기에서는 '제방이 터지다', '제방이 무너지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Children are playing on the riverbank embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제방'과 같은 뜻이지만 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '제방' but the easier, more everyday word.

phrases.en: The levee burst during the rainy season and the village flooded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물 때문에 제방이 갑자기 무너지는 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an accident where water suddenly breaks through a levee.

phrases.en: Residents built a levee along the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 막으려고 둑을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means building a bank to hold back water.

explain_en: It is a bank built to hold back river or sea water. In daily talk people often say '둑', while news and construction reports use phrases like '제방이 터지다' and '제방이 무너지다'.

t90.ax: Many people walk along the river embankment.

examples.en: At the zoo, a lion roared loudly.

examples.ko: 호랑이가 포효하는 소리가 산에 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The sound of a tiger roaring echoed through the mountain.
When the goal went in, the crowd cheered as if roaring.
The monster in the movie came running, roaring.
He was roaring, filled with anger.

examples.ko: 곰이 포효하자 아이들이 놀라서 뒤로 물러났어요.
examples.en: When the bear roared, the children were startled and stepped back.

explain: 사자나 호랑이 같은 맹수가 크게 울부짖는 것을 말해요. 사람에게 쓰면 화나 흥분으로 크게 소리 지르는 비유가 되고, 낮게 으르렁대는 '으르렁거리다'와는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.example: 사자가 크게 포효하자 아이들이 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: When the lion roared loudly, the children were startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크게'를 붙이면 소리가 얼마나 큰지 더 잘 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '크게' makes the loudness clearer.

phrases.en: I heard a tiger roaring from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미고, 울부짖는 소리 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' modifies the noun that follows and refers to the sound of the roar itself.

phrases.example: 개가 낯선 사람을 보고 낮게 으르렁거려요.
phrases.en: The dog growls low when it sees a stranger.
phrases.nuance_ko: '포효하다'는 크게 울부짖는 것이고, '으르렁거리다'는 낮고 위협하듯이 내는 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '포효하다' is a loud roar; '으르렁거리다' is a low, threatening growl.

explain_en: Animals roaring, or people roaring in a dramatic scene (사자가 포효하다) It describes big predators like lions and tigers letting out a loud cry. Used for people, it is figurative for shouting loudly in anger or excitement, and it feels different from '으르렁거리다', which is a lower growl.

t90.ax: At the zoo, a lion roared loudly.

examples.en: When spring comes, the river starts to thaw.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 해빙 분위기가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A thaw in relations has begun between the two countries.
During the thaw season, the roads are muddy and hard to drive on.

examples.ko: 두 회사 관계에도 해빙의 기미가 보여요.
examples.en: There are signs of a thaw in the relationship between the two companies too.

examples.ko: 이번 회담이 해빙을 앞당길 거라고 기대해요.
examples.en: I hope this meeting will bring the thaw sooner.

examples.ko: 해빙과 함께 얼음 아래 물고기들이 움직이기 시작해요.
examples.en: As the ice thaws, the fish under it begin to move.

explain: 얼음이 녹는 일 말고도 사이가 나빴던 나라나 사람의 관계가 풀리는 것을 비유로 말할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '해빙 무드', '해빙기'처럼 나와요. 반대로 관계가 얼어붙는 건 '냉각'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: During the thaw season, the river ice is thin and dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼음이 녹는 시기를 말하고, 관계가 풀리는 때에도 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The period when ice melts, also used figuratively for relations easing.

phrases.example: 두 나라 사이에 해빙 무드가 이어지고 있어요.
phrases.en: A thawing mood continues between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 나빴던 관계가 좋아지는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news for an atmosphere of improving relations.

phrases.example: 오랫동안 얼어붙은 두 나라의 관계가 해빙됐어요.
phrases.en: The long-frozen relationship between the two countries has thawed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼음이나 관계가 저절로 풀리는 것을 동사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form: ice or relations thawing on their own.

explain_en: Besides ice melting, it is used figuratively when the relationship between countries or people who were on bad terms starts to ease. In the news it shows up as '해빙 무드' and '해빙기'. The opposite, a relationship freezing over, is called '냉각'.

en: heating power; burning power; thermal power

examples.ko: 이 난로는 화력이 세서 방이 금방 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: This heater is powerful, so the room warms up quickly.

examples.ko: 화력이 약해서 물이 잘 안 끓어요.
examples.en: The heat is too weak, so the water will not boil.

examples.ko: 고기를 올릴 때는 화력을 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: Please lower the heat when you put the meat on.

examples.ko: 이 발전소는 석탄 화력으로 전기를 만들어요.
examples.en: This power plant makes electricity from burning coal.

examples.ko: 요리사는 화력에 따라 맛이 달라진다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The chef said the taste changes depending on the heat.

examples.ko: 캠핑장에서 숯불의 화력이 떨어져서 고기가 잘 안 익어요.
examples.en: The charcoal's heat dropped at the campsite, so the meat is not cooking well.

explain: 요리에서는 불의 세기를 말하는데, '센 불', '약한 불'이 더 일상적이에요. '화력이 세다/약하다', '화력을 줄이다/높이다'처럼 써요. 군대에서는 총과 대포의 공격력도 화력이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This gas stove has strong heating power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이나 기계의 열이 강하다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for saying a fire or machine produces strong heat.

phrases.en: Turn down the heat once the water boils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 불을 약하게 만드는 말이에요. 반대는 '화력을 높이다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in cooking to make the flame weaker; the opposite is '화력을 높이다'.

phrases.en: I quickly stir-fry the meat over high heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '화력이 세다'와 비슷한 뜻이지만 일상 요리에서는 '센 불'을 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '화력이 세다', but '센 불' is more common in everyday cooking talk.

explain_en: Heat strength of a stove, or weapons firepower. In cooking it is the strength of the flame, though '센 불' and '약한 불' are more everyday. Say '화력이 세다/약하다' or '화력을 줄이다/높이다'. In the military it also means the striking power of guns and cannons.

examples.en: When politicians make promises left and right, it's hard to believe them.
This shop hands out coupons far too freely.
A way of speaking that overuses foreign words is uncomfortable to hear.
We have to manage things so receipts aren't issued carelessly.
The company made promises recklessly, and the employees got worn out.
I used my credit cards too freely and my debt grew.

explain: 말, 약속, 쿠폰, 공약 등을 함부로 자꾸 내놓는다는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. '남용하다'는 권한이나 약을 지나치게 쓰는 것이고, '남발하다'는 무언가를 마구 내놓는 것이라 달라요. 피동 표현은 '남발되다'예요.

phrases.en: Fake news is being churned out far too much these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '남발하다'의 피동 표현으로, 무언가가 마구 나온다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 남발하다, used when things are being issued recklessly.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 약속을 남발해서 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: He makes promises too freely, so he's hard to trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지킬 생각 없이 약속을 자꾸 할 때 쓰는 나쁜 느낌의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a negative tone: making promises over and over without intending to keep them.

phrases.en: Please don't hand out coupons so freely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존댓말 부탁이나 충고에 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command used for requests or advice.

explain_en: It has a negative feeling of recklessly and repeatedly putting out words, promises, coupons or pledges. '남용하다' is overusing something like authority or medicine, while '남발하다' is handing things out carelessly, so they differ. The passive form is '남발되다'.

examples.en: When the power went out, the subway station fell into chaos.
The roads are in chaos because of the sudden snow.
The exam schedule changed, and great confusion broke out.
Right after the accident, the scene was total chaos.
I acted calmly even in the midst of the chaos.
The server stopped, and the reservations went into chaos.

explain: '혼란'보다 훨씬 크고 정신없는 상태예요. 보통 '대혼란에 빠지다, 대혼란이 일어나다, 대혼란을 겪다'로 써요. 반대로 질서가 있는 상태는 '질서'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The road fell into great chaos because of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 질서가 무너졌을 때 가장 많이 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression for when order suddenly breaks down.

phrases.en: Great chaos broke out at the concert hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼란이 갑자기 생겼다는 사실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state that chaos suddenly broke out.

phrases.example: 비행기가 취소되어 많은 사람이 대혼란을 겪었어요.
phrases.en: Many people went through great confusion because the flights were cancelled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 그 상황을 직접 경험했다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses that people personally went through the situation.

explain_en: It is a much bigger, more frantic state than '혼란'. It is usually used as '대혼란에 빠지다, 대혼란이 일어나다, 대혼란을 겪다'. The opposite state, with things in order, is '질서'.

examples.en: The farmers rose up in protest against the taxes.
We learned about the causes of the uprising in history class.
That uprising ended within a few days.

examples.ko: 시민 봉기가 나라를 바꾼 사례가 있어요.
examples.en: There are cases where a civil uprising changed a country.
People's anger eventually led to an uprising.

examples.ko: 봉기에 참여한 사람들의 이름이 기념비에 새겨졌어요.
examples.en: The names of the people who took part in the uprising were carved on the monument.

explain: 역사나 뉴스에서 억눌린 사람들이 한꺼번에 들고일어나는 일을 말해요. 비슷한 '시위'는 의견을 보여 주는 행동이고, '봉기'는 훨씬 격하게 맞서는 느낌이에요. '봉기를 일으키다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 역사 시간에 농민 봉기에 대해 배웠어요.
phrases.en: We learned about the peasant uprising in history class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 가장 자주 만나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The collocation you meet most often in history.

phrases.en: A big uprising broke out in 1894.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일으키다'는 하는 쪽, '일어나다'는 일이 벌어진 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 일으키다 focuses on those who start it; 일어나다 describes the event breaking out.

phrases.en: The citizens prepared an armed uprising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무기를 들고 맞서는 봉기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An uprising in which people take up arms.

explain_en: In history and news it means oppressed people rising up all at once. The similar '시위' (protest) is about showing an opinion, while '봉기' feels much more forceful. It is used as '봉기를 일으키다' (to stage an uprising).

examples.ko: 그는 억울하게 십 년이나 옥살이를 했어요.
examples.en: He spent ten years in prison unjustly.

examples.ko: 옥살이 끝에 풀려난 그분은 가족을 만나 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: After his time in prison, he was released and cried when he met his family.

examples.ko: 옥살이 때문에 그는 학교를 졸업하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of his time in prison, he couldn't graduate from school.

examples.ko: 옥살이에서 돌아온 뒤 그는 말수가 줄었어요.
examples.en: After coming back from prison, he became less talkative.

examples.ko: 짧은 옥살이였지만 그에게는 큰 상처가 됐어요.
examples.en: It was a short stint in prison, but it left a deep wound on him.
The independence activists endured long and hard years in prison.

explain: '감옥살이'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 보통 '옥살이를 하다, 옥살이를 겪다'처럼 말하고, 역사 이야기나 뉴스에서 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 그는 삼 년 동안 감옥살이를 했어요.
phrases.en: He spent three years in prison.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옥살이'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 쉽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 옥살이 but sounds a bit more plain.

phrases.en: He was imprisoned unjustly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation.

phrases.en: He went through a hard time in prison.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감옥에서 힘든 일을 당했다는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests he went through hardship while in prison.

explain_en: Everyday word for living through a prison term (옥살이를 하다) '감옥살이' is used with the same meaning. People usually say '옥살이를 하다' or '옥살이를 겪다', and you can hear it in history stories and the news.

t90.ax: He spent ten years in prison unjustly.

en: to be destroyed; to be ruined

examples.en: If you give in to greed, you end up ruined.
That company was ruined by debt.

examples.ko: 도박에 빠진 사람은 파멸할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person who falls into gambling can be ruined.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 우리 모두 파멸하고 말 거예요.
examples.en: If we go on like this, we will all end up ruined.

examples.ko: 그는 파멸하는 길인 줄 알면서도 멈추지 못했어요.
examples.en: He knew it was a path to ruin but could not stop.
They rebuilt the country that had gone to ruin.

explain: 돈, 건강, 관계, 나라처럼 큰 것이 완전히 무너져 다시 일어나기 힘들 때 써요. '실패하다'보다 훨씬 무겁고 되돌릴 수 없다는 느낌이 있어요. 주어는 사람, 회사, 나라가 올 수 있어요.

phrases.en: If you get hooked on gambling, you could be ruined.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길 수 있다고 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn that a bad outcome is possible.

phrases.en: He eventually reached ruin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파멸'이라는 명사와 같이 쓰는 말로, 끝내 무너진 상태가 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '파멸' and means reaching a final state of ruin.

phrases.en: That company collapsed because of debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파멸하다'와 비슷하지만 덜 무겁고 일상에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to '파멸하다' but lighter and used in everyday speech.

explain_en: A person's or group's life collapses; dramatic, written. Use it when something big, such as money, health, a relationship, or a country, collapses so completely that recovery is hard. It is much heavier than '실패하다' and carries a feeling that it cannot be undone. The subject can be a person, company, or country.

t90.ax: That company was ruined by debt.

en: to be touched deeply; to be emotional

examples.ko: 십 년 만에 고향 땅을 밟으니 감개무량해요.
examples.en: Setting foot in my hometown after ten years, I'm overwhelmed with emotion.
Seeing my parents on graduation day, I was deeply moved.
He accepted the award with a deeply moved expression.
My long-held dream has come true, and I'm truly overwhelmed.

examples.ko: 너무 감개무량해서 아무 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: I'm so moved that I can't say anything.

examples.ko: 이렇게 다 같이 모이니 감개무량하지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't it feel deeply moving to be all together like this?

explain: 오랜 세월이 지나 지난 일을 돌아보며 가슴이 벅찰 때 써요. 연설이나 인사말에서 자주 듣고, 가벼운 대화에서는 '뭉클하다', '감회가 새롭다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Tears came at that deeply moving moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤에 명사를 꾸며서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: Coming to school after so long, it stirs up feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛일을 떠올리며 느끼는 마음을 말하고, 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses feelings from recalling the past, and sounds more natural in conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel emotional about the past

phrases.en: Reading Mom's letter touches my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '감개무량하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to 감개무량하다.

explain_en: It is used when you look back on the past after a long time and feel your heart swell. You often hear it in speeches and greetings; in casual talk '뭉클하다' or '감회가 새롭다' sounds more natural.

en: to admire; to wonder; to be impressed

examples.en: Everyone marveled at the beautiful scenery.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래 실력에 저절로 감탄해요.
examples.en: I can't help marveling at that singer's skill.

examples.ko: 사람들은 그의 그림을 보고 감탄하며 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: People saw his painting and applauded in admiration.
It was food so delicious it made me marvel.
The teacher marveled at the student's fast progress.
Sounds of admiration could be heard here and there.

explain: 보통 '~에 감탄하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 대단하고 멋져서 저절로 소리가 나올 때 쓰고, 마음이 움직이는 '감동하다'와는 조금 달라요. 감탄하는 소리는 '와!' 같은 '감탄사'로 나와요.

phrases.en: The view was so nice that I couldn't help but exclaim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감탄이 저절로 나올 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for admiration slipping out naturally.
phrases.en_equiv: to let out an exclamation of admiration

phrases.en: I looked at the painting with an admiring face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감탄하는 모습을 뒤의 명사에 붙여 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a noun with a look of admiration.

phrases.en: Everyone watched the fireworks in admiration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감탄하면서 다른 행동을 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for doing something while admiring.

explain_en: Everyday; reacting with praise to skill or a good thing. It is usually used with the particle '에', as in '~에 감탄하다'. Use it when something is so impressive that you react spontaneously. It differs a little from '감동하다', being emotionally moved. The sound itself comes out as an interjection like '와!' (a '감탄사').

t90.ax: Everyone marveled at the beautiful scenery.
